updates.subject: Colorado Billing & Compensation Appendix
updates.rationale: Clarify service pay, separate conditional Tier 3 additions, and distinguish clinical-credit sick-leave accrual from the ten-minute H-code indirect allowance.
updates.changed_content:
Clinical Hour Rate currently covers approved 9-series clinical services at their assigned credit values. Standard Professional Rate currently covers approved H-code services at their documented hour or unit equivalents. Additional service codes may be assigned to either rate through a dated handbook update and an approved payroll mapping before use; a code prefix alone does not authorize a service or determine pay. Existing code-specific eligibility, indirect allowances and group restrictions continue to apply.

Clinical Hour Rate — approved 9-series services

Approved psychotherapy services, including 90832, 90834 and 90837, use the Clinical Hour Rate in the employee’s schedule. Family psychotherapy, psychotherapy add-ons, crisis services and group psychotherapy use their approved code-specific credit values and applicable authorization requirements. The “top” service rate is a category, not a promise of a full credit for every code. A 1.00-credit service pays the full credit rate; a 0.75-credit service pays 75% of that rate. No additional 20% indirect cash line is added to a clinical service-credit encounter.

Standard Professional Rate: H-code units and encounters in the app

Current app workflow. Payroll uses the services documented in the app. Use the employee’s applicable Standard Professional Rate and the code-specific basis below. A payer encounter is not automatically one hour of employee pay.

ServiceEmployee compensation basisDirect-pay formula
H0004 and other approved H-codes billed in 15-minute unitsVerified service units. One unit represents 0.25 compensation hour, even when actual service minutes differ.Units × 0.25 × applicable Standard Professional Rate.
H0031 and H0032, when billed per encounterActual documented service minutes, tabulated for payroll. The claim remains an encounter under the applicable payer rule.Documented service minutes ÷ 60 × applicable Standard Professional Rate.
Other H-codesThe approved code-specific mapping. Do not assume every H-code uses 15-minute units or that one encounter equals an hour.Use the dated mapping after billing/payroll verification.

Fifteen-minute unit boundaries

Where the applicable payer uses Colorado’s published 15-minute midpoint table: 8 through 22 minutes = 1 unit; 23 through 37 minutes = 2 units; 38 through 52 minutes = 3 units; 53 through 67 minutes = 4 units. Thus 23 minutes is two units, not one. Verify the payer, service-date rules, modifiers and authorized scope before billing; this compensation policy does not authorize a claim.

Included Indirect Service allowance

Integrated Services include Indirect Service time equal to 20% of compensated Direct Service time or its assigned time-equivalent, unless the Compensation Schedule expressly specifies another allowance. One direct hour includes 12 indirect minutes; 15 direct minutes include 3 indirect minutes. The included component is paid at the employee’s applicable Indirect Service Rate. Report qualifying excess work without duplicate payment.

Worked examples

At a $32 Standard Professional Rate and $22 Indirect Service Rate, one verified 15-minute compensation unit earns $8.00 direct and $1.10 included indirect; four units earn $32.00 direct and $4.40 included indirect. An encounter assigned 30 direct minutes earns $16.00 direct and $2.20 included indirect. Apply the service-specific Compensation Schedule and retain full precision until payroll aggregation.

Service-specific compensation method

The Compensation Schedule identifies whether each Integrated Service uses actual minutes, verified units, or a fixed encounter value. A software transition alone does not change the compensation method. Retain the method and effective date for each service date, including late-entered services.

Actual work and sick leave

Track actual direct, indirect and support work separately. Compensation units are not a substitute for actual-hours records. A service below a payer’s billing threshold or a delayed or denied claim does not erase pay for compensable work; report it for the appropriate payroll treatment. Payroll must reconcile minimum wage, overtime and other applicable wage requirements against actual work time. H-code direct compensation equivalents and paid indirect components enter the sick-leave calculation once; do not add the clinical-credit 1.20 multiplier. Reconcile against actual compensable hours and add any sick-leave accrual required by Colorado law.

Reference: Colorado behavioral health time documentation and unit rules. Billing must verify the current payer-specific requirements for the service date.

Actual time, payer units and internal credits

Record exact actual direct, indirect and support minutes separately from payer claim units and compensation credits. A qualifying 90837 maps to 1.00 compensation credit even when actual minutes differ from 60. Billing must follow the current payer’s requirements; a 53–74 minute example is not a universal maximum-duration rule. Verify scope, supervision, modifiers, place of service and telehealth rules for each service date. Never use leave-equivalent hours as actual hours worked.

Restricted and currently unapproved services

Any service delivered or billed as a group, regardless of its code, is subject to the group moratorium and requires express written approval before use. A saved payroll mapping is not permission to provide or bill a service. In particular, H2015, H2016, H2017 and H2018 require express written permission for any utilization. Their listing does not establish eligibility for group delivery; billing must verify current payer, setting and provider requirements. H2014 is permitted only through Skill Builders with express written approval, and is not approved for individual services. H0025 and H2032 are not currently approved.

H2018Express written permission required before any use. Any group delivery is subject to the group moratorium; payer and setting eligibility must be verified.

These are saved payroll mappings, not a payer fee schedule or certification of billability. Validate every mapping before activation. Required work remains compensable even if no claim can be submitted.

Probation and transition

Probation is at most 90 calendar days from original start, ends on an earlier manual waiver or achievement of Tier 3, and never restarts after Tier 3. Probation uses the disclosed minimum-workload rate in each pay category. Minimum-workload reductions are waived for 60 calendar days after the amendment’s prospective effective date. An October 10 effective date is protected through December 8; the reduction can first apply December 9. The waiver does not restart or extend probation. Track service dates across every rate boundary.

Versioned changes

Maintain the clinical-credit mappings, H-code indirect percentage and sick-leave ratio in the dated appendix. State the effective service date and provide written notice, plus agreement where required, before affected work. Preserve prior tables and signed schedules for late-entered services. Handbook edits alone do not enable payroll or reduce signed personal rates.

Category and level rate schedule

Clinical Hour Rate
The assigned credit value multiplied by your clinical rate. This covers approved 9-series clinical codes and designated master’s-level services in the appendix; it does not authorize every code beginning with 9. A 1.00-credit service pays the full rate and a 0.75-credit service pays 75%. Routine administrative work is included in this service pay. The 1.20 equivalent affects sick-leave accrual, not additional cash pay.
Standard Professional Rate
The rate used to calculate the Direct Service component of an Integrated Service from the service-specific minutes, units, or time-equivalent. The included indirect allowance is 20% of that direct time-equivalent, paid at the applicable Indirect Service Rate, unless the Compensation Schedule specifies another allowance.
Indirect Service Rate
The hourly rate used for the included indirect component and separately compensable qualifying Indirect Service. Do not submit the same included work twice. Qualifying excess work remains reportable and payable.
Support activity pay
The hourly rate for designated support activities, including required Provider Update review. Record actual compensable time.
Probationary and minimum-workload rates
Two distinct conditions that use the stated reduced rate: new-hire probation and the minimum-workload policy. Each has its own timing and exceptions, as described in the current Introductory Compensation and Minimum Workload Rate policies. A slash in the prior chart separated H-code and clinical rates; it did not combine them into one payment.
Levels and conditional bonuses
A compensation level selects the base rate within the credential category; it is separate from a workload/benefit tier. The chart’s “+” amount is conditional, not guaranteed and not included in base pay. The addition applies only when the employee qualifies for Tier 3 based on sessions per pay period.

updates.subject: Compensation levels: expectations, good standing and review
updates.rationale: Make compensation, service approval and benefit rules easy to find and understand.
updates.changed_content:
This section establishes the shared considerations for qualifying for, maintaining and reviewing compensation levels. The employee’s completed individual schedule identifies the assigned category, level and rates. These expectations take effect prospectively under the employee’s amendment and written notice; they do not create undisclosed retroactive criteria.

Annual paid event-work commitment

I agree to participate in a minimum of four (4) hours of assigned outreach or agency events during each calendar year, January 1 through December 31, compensated separately at my agreed-upon indirect hourly rate. While school-assigned, the annual commitment is eight (8) hours total, including four (4) additional hours for school-related events. The eight-hour total applies across all school assignments, not separately to each school. Actual event time is recorded and paid separately from service-credit compensation and automatic H-code indirect allowances; the same work may not be counted or paid twice.

ITSCO and the employee will identify and schedule the indirect duties that satisfy this commitment, including assigned outreach, community and school events. Required outreach under this commitment is paid indirect work, not unpaid volunteering. Other activities retain the pay classification disclosed in the compensation schedule unless expressly designated as part of this indirect-work assignment. The commitment does not automatically add four or eight hours to payroll: record all actual time worked, including additional compensable time. ITSCO will make assignments and scheduling expectations clear. Management will address unavailable assignments, school closures, approved schedule changes, protected leave and reasonable accommodations; an employee will not be treated as failing this commitment solely because ITSCO did not make the work available. Requirements are adjusted as required for protected leave and accommodations, without unpaid make-up work. Applicable minimum wage and overtime protections continue to apply.

Evaluation categories

1. Annual paid event-work commitment

Complete the assigned four-hour annual event commitment, or eight-hour annual total while school-assigned (January 1–December 31), with accurate actual-time records and timely follow-through. Review both the work made available and the work performed; do not substitute automatic payroll allowances for actual participation.

Review evidence: Assigned duties, agreed schedules, time records and completed work, with approved adjustments documented.

2. Documentation quality and timeliness

Complete accurate notes, treatment plans and required documentation within the communicated clinical, payer and agency deadlines. Correct errors and respond to documentation requests promptly. Review system outages, approved extensions and protected absences before identifying a performance concern.

Review evidence: Applicable deadlines, completion records, accuracy reviews and the employee’s explanation of barriers.

3. Attendance, call-offs and clinician cancellations

Meet agreed schedules, give timely notice when unable to attend, and support appropriate client notification, rescheduling and coverage. Consider avoidable clinician cancellations and unprotected attendance concerns in context. Exclude protected leave and accommodations; distinguish clinician decisions from client cancellations, school closures and events outside the employee’s control.

Review evidence: Scheduling and notice records, reasons for cancellations, coverage efforts and confirmed circumstances.

4. Outreach and team participation

Participate in assigned outreach events and practice or school partnership activities that fit the employee’s role and disclosed schedule. Communicate conflicts and complete agreed alternatives when appropriate. Assigned outreach hours under this commitment are paid at the agreed indirect rate and count toward the four- or eight-hour calendar-year total; additional actual work remains compensable.

Review evidence: Event assignments, participation, completed follow-up and documented scheduling arrangements.

5. Professional standing, collaboration and feedback

Maintain required credentials and supervision, follow professional and agency standards, communicate respectfully and address substantiated concerns. Consider reports from schools, clients and staff after reviewing facts, context and the employee’s response. A complaint alone is not a finding of misconduct or an automatic basis for a lower level. Good-faith reporting, wage concerns and other protected activity are not adverse factors.

Review evidence: Credential and supervision records, specific observed conduct, documented feedback and reviewed findings.

6. Client connection and engagement

Build a responsive, respectful therapeutic relationship; communicate appropriately with clients and authorized caregivers; and address access, language and engagement barriers within the employee’s role. Evaluate the clinician’s actions and quality of care, with attention to client choice and confidentiality, rather than popularity or retention alone.

Review evidence: Appropriate feedback, communication and follow-up records, care coordination and documented engagement efforts.

7. Treatment goals, progress and appropriate completion of care

Develop individualized goals and objectives, assess progress, adjust care when needed, and support clinically appropriate goal attainment, termination, transfer or referral. Consider client acuity, readiness, disability, school context and other barriers. Progress is a consideration, not a guaranteed outcome. Do not reward unnecessary treatment, premature discharge, selecting only easier cases or a predetermined number of successful terminations.

Review evidence: Clinical review of treatment planning, progress assessment, appropriate adjustments and continuity-of-care decisions.

8. School and client action items

Complete assigned intake, family contact, school coordination, roster, scheduling and other client action items by communicated deadlines. Keep status records accurate and escalate blocked items promptly. Apply school-specific responsibilities only while school-assigned and within authorized information-sharing boundaries.

Review evidence: Task assignments, due dates, completion records, escalations and documented external dependencies.

Evaluation schedule and good standing

ITSCO will conduct formal compensation-level evaluations one to two times per year. Supervisors may provide feedback and address concerns between formal evaluations. Reviews consider the responsibilities applicable to the employee’s role, the expectations disclosed in advance, reliable evidence and the employee’s response. Good standing means substantially meeting the applicable professional, documentation, reliability, participation and follow-through expectations, with concerns assessed fairly and in context. Protected leave, reasonable accommodations and other protected activity are excluded from adverse consideration.

For each applicable category, document “Meets expectations,” “Needs improvement” or “Not applicable,” with the review period, supporting facts and the employee’s comments. Disclose role- or level-specific standards before using them. This framework does not establish undisclosed point totals, weighting or automatic promotion/demotion thresholds.

Maintaining or changing a compensation level

A review may result in maintaining the current compensation level, advancement when the applicable criteria are met, or a prospective reduction within the employee’s compensation category when documented expectations are not met. Advancement is not automatic. Management will communicate the reasons, relevant evidence and expectations for improvement, ordinarily with a written improvement plan and a follow-up date; serious concerns may require earlier action. The employee may submit a response or request management review. Any changed level and resulting rates must be communicated in writing before affected work, with any agreement required by existing terms. No review reduces pay or leave already earned. A handbook edit, complaint, missed task or app-generated flag does not automatically change an employee’s pay level. Credential categories and session-based workload tiers remain distinct from performance-based compensation levels; Tier 3 bonus eligibility continues to follow the disclosed session-count rules.

Clinical decisions must prioritize appropriate care and client choice. Reviewers must not use treatment outcomes or discharge counts as quotas. Share only the information appropriate for the review; detailed clinical records remain in the authorized clinical record.

Supervisory review and evaluations

Supervisory reviews, clinical documentation reviews and formal performance evaluations are also considered when determining whether an employee meets the expectations for their compensation level. Findings must be documented, reviewed in context and discussed with the employee.

updates.subject: Sick-leave accrual ratio for fee-for-service staff
updates.rationale: Clarify annual paid event participation, current sick-leave rates, activity classifications and prospective compensation policies.
updates.changed_content:
Initial ratio: 20% administrative equivalent

Clinical credits × 1.20 ÷ 30 = sick-leave hours earned. The direct bucket receives 1.00 equivalent hour per credit and the administrative bucket receives 0.20. Thus 25 credits = 30 equivalent hours = 1 hour of sick leave; 0.75 credit = 0.90 equivalent hour = 0.03 sick-leave hour. The administrative equivalent affects accrual only for psychotherapy credit services and is already included in service pay.

Integrated Direct Service time and its included Indirect Service time enter the accrual calculation once. Under the standard 20% allowance, one direct hour plus 0.20 included indirect hour equals 1.20 accrual hours. Do not apply another clinical-credit multiplier to that total. Separately compensated Indirect Service, Support Activity, and qualifying Excess Time also count without duplication. Reconcile against all actual compensable work and apply any required sick-leave shortfall.

This remains protected paid sick leave, not a new vacation bank. It accrues without a probation waiting period and is paid using the highest currently eligible rate under the sick-leave pay policy. Payroll applies the HFWA calculation rules for the leave dates, using the currently applicable clinical per-credit or direct hourly base rate, excluding Tier 3 additions and other bonuses or differentials. Preserve existing balances and more generous earned terms. HFWA generally requires at least one hour per 30 hours worked up to 48 annually, with applicable carryover up to 48 hours; protected uses, reasonable notice, permitted documentation and nonretaliation requirements apply. Do not apply a generic 10-hour rollover cap or 30-day notice rule to protected sick leave.

ITSCO may update the ratio prospectively through the dated handbook appendix and corresponding payroll policy version, with notice and any required agreement. Preserve accrued balances and historical service calculations. AI documentation does not change the ratio automatically or remove pay for required review and correction. Actual work remains compensable even with a zero allowance. Any separate vacation/general PTO entitlement retains its existing protections.

updates.subject: Actual time, support activities and corrections
updates.rationale: Clarify annual paid event participation, current sick-leave rates, activity classifications and prospective compensation policies.
updates.changed_content:
The Workplace Handbook identifies activities eligible for indirect pay and support-activity pay. These activity types will be added to the web application as needed. ITSCO reserves the right to designate activities as indirect work or support activities and to add, revise or reclassify activity types prospectively. The applicable classification and rate will be communicated before the work is performed. Record actual compensable time under the designated activity; a missing app option should be reported for entry or correction. A later classification change does not reduce pay already earned or permit duplicate payment.

Record all compensable work daily. Provider Update active review time is tracked by session and section and submitted for payroll review at the applicable support activity rate. Paused, hidden and timed-out periods are not automatically credited; report legitimate unrecorded work through a correction request. Actual work beyond an allowance remains compensable.

Clinical credits and automatic indirect equivalents are not substitutes for actual time records. Apply applicable minimum wage, overtime, rest-period and regular-rate rules, including workweek and daily requirements. A late note, missing preapproval or denied claim does not erase earned wages. Handle documentation or approval concerns separately from paying for work performed.

Clinical supervision compensation

Clinical supervision is paid at the supervisor’s individually negotiated or contracted hourly rate. This handbook does not set a universal supervision dollar rate.

Assigned responsibilityCompensation basis
Direct clinical supervision100% of the contracted supervision hourly rate
Hosting group clinical supervision150% of the contracted supervision hourly rate
Reviewing and co-signing another provider’s notes50% of the contracted supervision hourly rate per actual note-review hour

Group pay is based on actual hosting time, not the number of participants. Note-review pay covers actual time reviewing and co-signing another provider’s notes, not the supervisor’s own notes. Record review time separately without duplicate payment or an automatic allowance per supervision hour. Paused and inactive time is excluded from automatic tracking; report legitimate work the tracker misses for correction. Tracked time remains under payroll review until accepted and applied. The supervisor’s individual agreement identifies their contracted rate.

updates.subject: Group services: moratorium, Skill Builders and exceptions
updates.rationale: Make compensation, service approval and benefit rules easy to find and understand.
updates.changed_content:
Any service delivered or billed as a group, regardless of its code, is subject to the group moratorium and requires express written approval before use. A saved payroll mapping is not permission to provide or bill a service. In particular, H2015, H2016, H2017 and H2018 require express written permission for any utilization. Their listing does not establish eligibility for group delivery; billing must verify current payer, setting and provider requirements. H2014 is permitted only through Skill Builders with express written approval, and is not approved for individual services. H0025 and H2032 are not currently approved.

Current group moratorium, including 90853

New provider-initiated groups are paused practice-wide, including psychotherapy groups billed under 90853 and groups using H-codes. Approved Skill Builders programming may continue within its existing authorization. Other groups require a written exception before advertising, enrolling or scheduling. Coordinate safe continuity of care for existing clients; this policy does not direct abrupt cancellation of care.

Submitting a group proposal

Staff may propose a group to Michael and Rachel. Include its clinical purpose, participant needs and acuity, payer/RAE coverage, proposed codes, treatment-plan requirements, curriculum, staffing and supervision, schedule, expected attendance, supplies and all preparation, documentation, delivery and cleanup time. Support and billing must confirm eligibility, authorizations and the applicable reimbursement and billing restrictions.

Compensation and wage requirements

A proposal will not be approved if there is a reasonable likelihood that the compensation plan would fail to pay any employee at least the applicable minimum wage for all compensable work. Include low attendance, cancellations, preparation and follow-up time in the budget. ITSCO must fund any legally required wage or overtime adjustment even if reimbursement is less than expected. An employee cannot agree to waive these protections.

Compensation different from an employee’s usual rates may be set in an individual written agreement before the work begins. That agreement must state the work, pay method and rates, and comply with applicable minimum wage, overtime, recordkeeping and other employment requirements. Payer denials, delayed payment or low attendance do not cancel wages already earned.

Why groups require review

Recent Medicaid changes at the federal and state levels, broad funding and reimbursement cuts, and correspondence from CCHA, Rocky Mountain Health Plans and Colorado Access have created uncertainty about service coverage, reimbursement and program sustainability. These changes affect how ITSCO plans and funds care, including group and H-code services.

Changes to eligibility and renewal requirements may cause some parents or guardians to lose Medicaid coverage or experience gaps in coverage. The effects can extend to family finances, access to care and continuity of treatment, even when a child remains eligible. A parent’s loss of coverage does not automatically mean their child has lost coverage; staff should help families verify their individual status and coordinate care.

In response, ITSCO is maintaining the group moratorium and written-review process while evaluating the effects of these changes. Proposals must account for current coverage and reimbursement, likely attendance, and all staffing, preparation, documentation and supervision costs so that services remain sustainable and all work is properly compensated.

updates.subject: Digital workplace and transition procedures
updates.rationale: Forms, documentation, scheduling and timekeeping now use the app throughout both handbooks. Earlier external-system and future-cutover instructions are superseded.
updates.changed_content:
The app is the workplace system of record. Complete internal forms, requests, scheduling, clinical documentation, supervision records, evaluations, timekeeping and payroll submissions in the app. Use the appropriate record or assigned workflow; do not submit parallel Google Forms, external time logs, spreadsheets or emailed timesheets.

Record actual service and work time, review tracked entries, and submit missing time or corrections through the app. A missing tracking option does not make work unpaid. If a needed workflow is unavailable, report the issue through in-app support so the record can be completed or corrected.

Use authorized in-app communication and respect notification and texting preferences. Protect confidential information and use only approved recipient and access settings. Quick View access requires an individual protected code and a secure device. Emergency calls and required external reports must not be delayed while completing an app record; document the actions in the app as soon as it is safe.

updates.subject: Workplace Handbook and update tracker in the app
updates.rationale: Keep the current handbook and its communicated changes accessible together in the app.
updates.changed_content:
Read the current Workplace Handbook and Handbook Updates in the app. Each update identifies its current policy locations; select a policy title to open that exact handbook section. Effective dates remain part of the applicable policy. Sections whose full source has not yet been transferred are labeled Text pending.

Published versions and update history retain prior wording for reference. The current handbook contains the reconciled replacement policy, and later handbook publications record the section changes in the latest Handbook Updates draft.

updates.subject: Spanish-language intake and handoff
updates.rationale: Give staff a clear shared procedure in the app and handbook.
updates.changed_content:
Record the client’s and parent/guardian’s primary languages separately in the app’s intake record and client profile. When a parent or guardian prefers Spanish, arrange a Spanish-speaking parent intake through the agency’s Spanish intake team.

  1. Request availability: Open Messages by Conversa and choose the Spanish / Español group. Request a parent-intake time without posting identifying clinical information to the group.
  2. Assign the Spanish-speaking provider: Support coordinates the handoff and adds that provider to the individual client’s authorized care team. Group membership alone does not grant access to client records.
  3. Complete the intake: The Spanish-speaking provider conducts the parent intake and completes its documentation in the client record. The primary provider may attend if helpful.
  4. Prepare the care summary: The primary provider uses the Note Aid treatment-summary workflow to prepare a brief, relevant summary, reviews it for accuracy, and saves the reviewed summary in the authorized medical record. The assigned Spanish-speaking provider accesses it there.
  5. Continue coordination: The assigned Spanish-speaking provider handles future parent check-ins and coordination of care, documenting contacts and sharing relevant updates with the primary provider through the client record.
  6. When coverage is unavailable: Ask support to arrange appropriate language assistance. Do not use children as interpreters or treat an unsuccessful English-language contact as a refusal of services.

In your Provider Update, list languages you can use proficiently enough to conduct sessions and select your proficiency. Update support when your availability changes.

updates.subject: Business cards and public profiles
updates.rationale: Give staff a clear shared procedure in the app and handbook.
updates.changed_content:
You can print your own ITSCO business cards at the office. Preprinted cardstock with the ITSCO website QR code will be available, so you can print your provider information on the other side.

How to print

  1. Check your profile first. Open your public provider profile from the Provider Update and make sure your name, credentials, photo, contact information, and profile link are correct.
  2. Open the business card template in the app and use the current version.
  3. Get the cardstock. Preprinted business-card cardstock is located in the right drawer of the kitchen desk.
  4. Use the color Brother printer on the back side of the kitchen desk. The printer can only take one sheet at a time.
  5. Load the cardstock with the QR-code side facing up so the QR code is readable when you look at it.
  6. In the printer settings, set Print Quality to Great instead of Good and Paper Type to Matte Photo Paper. Click OK.
  7. Print one sheet first. Check that your information is correct and everything is properly aligned before printing additional cards.
  8. Once the test sheet looks correct, print additional sheets one at a time.

The preprinted QR code links to the main ITSCO website. If needed, the cards can also be printed on both sides.

Please use the current app-generated template and do not add a private care-texting number or other personal contact information that is not intended for public use.

If your profile information is incorrect or you have trouble with the template, printer, or alignment, use Need help in the Provider Update to submit a Technology support ticket before continuing. You can attach screenshots. General ITSCO support: support@itsco.health.

updates.subject: Office kiosk and client arrivals
updates.rationale: Give staff a clear shared procedure in the app and handbook.
updates.changed_content:
The new office kiosk brings client check-in and office information together in one place.

  • Client check-in: Clients select their provider and appointment time, confirm who is checking in, and let the provider know they have arrived. If an appointment is missing, they can use “Message our support team” or ask the office team for help.
  • Arrival notifications: The kiosk records the client’s arrival and sends an in-app notification to the provider. Depending on notification settings, text or email alerts may also be available. Check the app for arrivals.
  • Today’s providers: View provider office hours and room information.
  • Office directory: Find rooms and view the office layout.
  • Provider profiles: View current provider photos and public profile information. Please keep your photo, biography, and focus areas up to date through your Provider Update.
  • Programs & events: View available office programs and events. Program-specific check-in or clock-in/out options will only appear where configured.
  • Visit forms & feedback: Complete assigned visit questionnaires or feedback after check-in. Optional feedback can be skipped and will not prevent check-in. Authorized providers can review saved responses and available trends.

The kiosk will return to the welcome screen after completion or inactivity. Please finish or clear the screen before leaving it and let staff know if any information appears incorrect.

The kiosk is intended for arrival and office information only. It is not used to start care or report an emergency.

Open the kiosk entry · Staff can open the configured office kiosk; clients should use the device provided at their office.

updates.subject: Minimum-workload rates and tracking
updates.rationale: Make compensation, service approval and benefit rules easy to find and understand.
updates.changed_content:
Effective November 13, 2026, eligibility for the applicable Standard Professional Rate requires at least:

12 Workload Clinical Hours during each standard 14-day pay period.

If the Employee completes fewer than 12 Workload Clinical Hours, the Practice provides one 14-day grace period.

If the Employee remains below the threshold after the grace period, the applicable Minimum Workload Rate begins prospectively with the following pay period.

The Minimum Workload Rate does not retroactively reduce compensation already earned.

FFS Services

For FFS Clinical Hour Services, the Minimum Workload Rate temporarily replaces the Employee's regular Clinical Hour Rate.

The service's Clinical Hour Value does not change.

Integrated Services

For Integrated Services, the Minimum Workload Rate temporarily replaces the applicable Standard Professional Rate used to calculate the Direct Service Component only.

The Employee's:

  • Indirect Service Rate;
  • Included Indirect percentage;
  • Support Activity Rate; and
  • separately approved Excess Indirect compensation

are not reduced solely because the Minimum Workload Rate applies.

Minimum-workload rate schedule

CategoryClinical Hour RateStandard Professional RateIndirect paySupport activity pay
Category 1$22.00 per clinical credit$22.00 per H-code direct-hour equivalent$18 at Levels 1–2; $20 at Levels 3–5 per hour$18 per hour
Category 2$38.00 per clinical credit$25.00 per H-code direct-hour equivalent$22 per hour$18 per hour
Category 3$45.00 per clinical credit$25.00 per H-code direct-hour equivalent$24 per hour$18 per hour

The service compensation schedule identifies the applicable category and level. The included indirect percentage, Indirect Service Rate, and Support Activity Rate are not reduced by minimum-workload status. Review and request corrections in My Payroll.

Tier 3 lookback exemption

Effective November 13, 2026, an Employee who has achieved Tier 3 status during at least one of the preceding six completed pay periods is exempt from application of the Minimum Workload Rate solely because workload falls below the minimum threshold.

The exemption applies while the Employee continues to meet the applicable Tier 3 lookback requirement.

Tier calculations are governed by the Practice's applicable workload policies.

updates.subject: Service codes: Clinical Session Rate and Direct Care Rate
updates.rationale: Make compensation, service approval and benefit rules easy to find and understand.
updates.changed_content:
Clinical Hour Rate currently covers approved 9-series clinical services at their assigned credit values. Standard Professional Rate currently covers approved H-code services at their documented hour or unit equivalents. Additional service codes may be assigned to either rate through a dated handbook update and an approved payroll mapping before use; a code prefix alone does not authorize a service or determine pay. Existing code-specific eligibility, included indirect allowances and group restrictions continue to apply.

Use this reference with your individual pay schedule. A code in a payroll mapping is not permission to perform every service under that code. Services must fit your credentials, supervision, client plan and payer requirements. Unlisted services require written review before use. Group use of any code remains subject to the separate moratorium.

Clinical Hour Rate — approved 9-series codes and credits

Clinical Hour Rate equals assigned clinical credits multiplied by your Clinical Hour Rate. A qualifying 90837 earns 1.00 credit; 90834 earns 0.75; 90832 earns 0.50. Credits measure compensation, not actual hours. Codes such as 99414–99416 used for separately recorded supervision/administrative time are not clinical psychotherapy credits merely because they begin with 9.

Restricted and currently unapproved services

Any service delivered or billed as a group, regardless of its code, is subject to the group moratorium and requires express written approval before use. How quantities are categorized

updates.subject: School mileage reimbursement
updates.rationale: Make compensation, service approval and benefit rules easy to find and understand.
updates.changed_content:
This policy outlines how eligible employees may request and receive mileage reimbursement for travel to approved school locations. Mileage reimbursement is a discretionary benefit, not a guaranteed entitlement, and is governed by the Practice’s Benefit Tier Framework and operational considerations.

Eligibility, reimbursement rates, and caps may be modified or discontinued at any time.

Eligibility & Tier Levels

Mileage reimbursement eligibility is determined by the employee’s assigned Benefit Tier at the time of submission:

  • Tier 1: No mileage reimbursement
  • Tier 2: $0.35 per eligible mile
  • Tier 3: $0.70 per eligible mile

Mileage reimbursement is subject to an annual reimbursement cap of $2,000 per employee, unless otherwise approved in writing. This cap may be adjusted, suspended, or eliminated at the Practice’s discretion.

Claim Process

Record the travel date, assigned school, originating office, eligible route, and miles in My Payroll → Mileage. Use the school-travel option and assigned office; explain any manual-distance correction. Submit by the Sunday after the pay period closes. Other business mileage requires prior approval.

Payroll reviews the applicable tier and eligible miles. A zero optional benefit rate does not remove reimbursement required by law. Request review of a missing route, incorrect distance, or eligibility decision.

Calculation Method

  • Commute Deduction: Reimbursement is calculated based on the roundtrip distance from the employee’s home to the assigned school location minus the roundtrip distance from the employee’s home to their designated office location (Windchime or Broadway).
  • School Locations Only: Only services that actually occurred at school sites are eligible under this policy.
  • Multiple School Locations: If an employee travels to multiple schools in a single day, reimbursement is calculated using only the single school farthest from the employee’s home. Additional travel between schools is not separately reimbursable.
  • Closer Locations: If the assigned school is closer to the employee’s home than the designated office, no mileage reimbursement will be issued for that trip.

Payment & Processing

  • Payroll Integration: Approved mileage reimbursement will be processed through the employee’s regular paycheck.
  • Tax Treatment: Mileage reimbursement is treated as taxable income and subject to applicable payroll taxes.
  • Paystub Display: Approved amounts will appear as “Mileage Reimbursement” on the employee’s paystub.

Example

An employee lives 12 miles roundtrip from the Windchime office.

The assigned school is 17 miles roundtrip from the employee’s home.

Difference: 5 miles

At Tier 2 (50%):

5 miles × $0.35 = $1.75

At Tier 3 (100%):

5 miles × $0.70 = $3.50

Compliance and Oversight

Employees are responsible for accurate mileage reporting and ensuring that all addresses used for calculation are correct. Mileage claims must align with services documented in the app.

Any misrepresentation or inconsistency may result in denial of reimbursement and/or corrective action.

Modification or Discontinuation

ITSCO may change mileage eligibility, rates, caps, or availability prospectively with notice. Changes do not remove reimbursement already earned or required by law.

updates.subject: Training leave — separate from sick leave
updates.rationale: Document the 0.25-per-30 training benefit for all employees, with separate eligibility and carryover rules.
updates.changed_content:
Training PTO is paid time earned for approved professional development and training. All hours and service-credit equivalents that qualify for sick-leave accrual also qualify for training accrual, including fee-for-service and salaried employees’ eligible work. The rate is 0.25 training hour per 30 qualifying hours or credits. Use the same documented qualifying basis as sick leave, including applicable clinical-credit equivalents; do not add an equivalent twice.

Training PTO is restricted to approved training and may not be converted to general PTO. It pays at the employee’s applicable sick-leave payment rate for the use date. Required employer training remains paid work even if this benefit has no available balance.

Tracking, cap and ADP handoff

People Operations enters or confirms the current ADP training balance in the app, together with the last completed pay period included in that balance. The app then accrues subsequent eligible periods without counting imported hours again. Staff view their balance and requests in My Payroll. Unused training hours carry forward until used. Accrual pauses at a 20-hour balance cap and resumes after approved use; a cap does not erase an existing balance.

Requesting Training PTO

In My Payroll, choose Training PTO, enter the training date and hours, provide a brief description, enter the training cost and upload a receipt, signup confirmation or proof of participation. People Operations may request further participation documentation. ITSCO may deny a request if sufficient documentation is not provided. The balance is deducted only when payroll approves the request and applies its payment. Pending or denied requests do not reduce the earned balance. A separate expense reimbursement requires its own approval; reporting a course cost does not automatically create a second payment.

See Continuing Education in the Employee Benefits Overview for additional approval and reimbursement requirements. Training leave is separate from protected sick leave and school support activity hours.

updates.subject: School support activity hours
updates.rationale: Track school support hours on the shared sick-leave basis, with a 20-hour cap and payroll-approved use.
updates.changed_content:
School-assigned employees earn a separate bank of support activity hours. All work hours and service-credit equivalents that qualify for sick-leave accrual count toward this bank while school-assigned, including eligible work outside schools. The rate is 2 support activity hours per 25 qualifying hours or credits. Use the same documented qualifying basis as sick leave and count each component once. Thirty qualifying hours earn 2.4 support activity hours. The bank is separate from sick leave and Training PTO.

Purpose — weather disruptions and missed sessions

This earned benefit is earmarked to help school-assigned providers cover time lost to weather-related school closures or disruptions and missed client sessions, including client absences or cancellations. It is separate from sick leave and Training PTO, and is paid at the employee’s applicable support-activity rate.

Payment is limited to earned available hours and the handbook’s request and payroll-approval requirements. It is not an automatic payment for every missed appointment and does not replace wages for work actually performed. Existing earned balances and previously approved uses remain protected.

Balance and use

The app displays the balance as support activity hours, such as “2 support activity hours” or “10 support activity hours.” Accrual pauses at a 20-hour balance cap and resumes after approved use. Track earnings by calendar year, January–December, but preserve earned unused balances rather than forfeiting them at year-end. Because use requires a date rather than a qualifying event, the applicable earned-vacation protections apply regardless of the bank’s name.

In My Payroll, choose Request support activity hours and enter the use date and number of hours. No explanation or receipt is required. Payroll checks the balance, applicable support-activity rate and payment period. Only approval and successful application to payroll deduct the hours. Pending or denied requests do not reduce the earned balance. Pay equals approved hours multiplied by the employee’s applicable support-activity hourly rate.

The app retains source periods, qualifying hours, accruals, approvals and deductions for audit. The balance will not be sent to ADP as a leave bank; payments still appear in normal payroll, tax and wage records. This benefit replaces future school Medicaid no-show compensation from its configured transition date, while preserving amounts earned under the previous policy. Do not claim both benefits for the same event.

updates.subject: Consistent compensation across funding sources
updates.rationale: Make compensation, service approval and benefit rules easy to find and understand.
updates.changed_content:
Beginning on this amendment’s effective date, I will be compensated at the applicable rates in my individual compensation schedule for the services and duties I perform, regardless of the payment or funding source. This includes insurance, self-pay, grants, iMatter and other externally funded programs or contracts. My compensation is based on the approved service, credits or hours and assigned duties, rather than a percentage of the amount billed, collected or reimbursed. For work covered by this amendment, these terms replace prior funding-specific percentage or revenue-sharing compensation arrangements. Applicable approved differentials and separately stated role or duty rates continue to apply. This change applies prospectively after the required signatures and does not reduce compensation already earned.

Rationale

Funding arrangements have changed over time, and some external contracts have omitted provider-compensation terms or applied them inconsistently. Using each employee’s agreed service and duty rates provides a consistent basis for compensation across programs. Differences in a program’s reimbursement do not create an automatic increase or decrease in the employee’s rate.

For example, a covered 1.00-credit clinical service pays the employee’s agreed per-credit rate whether funded by insurance, a grant or iMatter. It is not paid as 50% of a program’s reimbursement under this amendment. Salaried employees remain subject to their salary agreements. Approved supervision, mentoring and other assigned-duty rates remain governed by the employee’s individual schedule. Any separate group-work compensation must be agreed in writing under the group-review policy.

Payroll must retain the prior arrangement for earlier service dates and apply the new method only from the completed amendment’s prospective effective date. Editing the handbook alone does not change an existing signed agreement or activate a percentage-pay override.

updates.subject: Health Insurance — employee-only employer contribution
updates.rationale: Clarify that the agency contribution is based on employee-only coverage and employees pay the additional cost of dependent coverage.
updates.changed_content:
Basis of the agency contribution

For eligible employees enrolled in agency-sponsored health insurance, the agency contribution is based on the premium for employee-only coverage and the contribution percentage or amount applicable to the employee’s benefit eligibility. Enrollment in employee-plus-spouse, employee-plus-child or family coverage does not increase the agency contribution. The agency does not contribute toward the additional cost of dependent coverage.

Employee responsibility and dependent enrollment

The employee pays the portion of the employee-only premium not covered by the agency contribution, plus the full additional premium for enrolled dependents. Eligible dependents may still enroll when permitted by the plan; this policy limits the agency’s premium contribution and does not exclude dependents from coverage. It does not promise payment of the employee’s full premium.

Where to review your benefit

Review My Benefits → Health Insurance in the app for enrollment information, the applicable employer contribution and benefit eligibility. People Operations maintains the employee-only premium used to calculate the contribution, separately from any additional dependent premium. Contact People Operations if the displayed premium includes family coverage or differs from the carrier’s employee-only amount.

The governing plan documents and applicable law control coverage, eligibility, enrollment and administration. Any change affecting an existing contribution arrangement must be applied prospectively with required notice and any required agreement; this handbook update does not itself change payroll deductions or an existing signed agreement.

updates.subject: Practice-provided liability and clinical malpractice insurance
updates.changed_content: The Practice provides liability insurance and clinical malpractice insurance for its authorized operations, including authorized clinical work performed by employees and clinical students/interns. Coverage is subject to the applicable insurance policy terms and the individual’s authorized role and supervision. This handbook does not extend coverage to unrelated outside activities or promise coverage for work performed before joining the Practice. Request a certificate of insurance or clarification of coverage from People Operations through the app.
updates.rationale: October 10 owner confirmation: the companies provide liability and clinical malpractice insurance, including clinical student placements. Replaces the prior malpractice exclusion. Carrier, limits and individual claim determinations are not asserted.
